scope: Read actual frozen model/teacher/evidence/trainer, existing native-target builder, actual run config/logs, and one existing word/target cache pair. No model pass, new test, scoring or loss change.
objective: L = L_generation + lambda * mean((C - T_reasoning_words)^2) / target_scale^2
equivalent_residual_form: For C = C_anchor + delta, L_sem = ||delta - (T - C_anchor)||^2 / (N * target_scale^2), delta = shared_offset + PZ.
confirmed_facts: Native targets encode each reasoning relation separately with frozen official T5 and Wan text embedding; no separate literal-request or image target is constructed. Reasoning text can itself carry information from those inputs.
R9/R9.1 reader adds literal request features; content_loss still resamples native_words belonging to the reasoning relations.
The full C receives per-slot MSE; both shared_offset and PZ receive its gradient. The loss does not label which difference helps physical generation.
Resampling linearly interpolates the actual lexical sequence to64 slots in each of4 relations. It does not replicate one sentence mean64 times.
Actual lambda reaches.03 at step32 and stays.03 through400 because decay_start600 is beyond this budget; final_weight.015 is not reached.
R1 used the same objective and matched schedule. These facts alone do not establish why R9.1 performs worse or that removing the auxiliary would improve PC.

one_observed_cache_example.native_teacher: official frozen T5 then official Wan text_embedding
one_observed_cache_example.interpretation: Scope describes input provenance; the target encoder itself reads relation texts.34 original word features are interpolated to256 targets; this is one example, not a corpus statistic.

hypothesis_for_later_review: Full-vector lexical reconstruction may oppose request-specific or image-context-specific generation corrections that are not represented in the lexical target. Native semantic alignment can still help and R1 already benefits; actual gradient conflict and the effect of changing the loss remain unmeasured.
